issues.legal_issue: Statutory vesting of excess land does not by itself transfer actual possession from the landholder.
material_facts: The land was notified as excess and treated as vested in the government.
A notice directed the landholder to surrender possession and warned that force could be used if possession was not surrendered.
The landholder did not voluntarily surrender possession, and the officials’ affidavits and the record disclosed no proof of peaceful or forcible possession being taken under the statutory procedure.
A possession receipt recording a later transfer of the land to a development authority was executed without notice to the landholder.
issues.conclusion: The statutory vesting transferred title and de jure possession, but not de facto possession. Because neither voluntary surrender nor lawful peaceful or forcible dispossession was established, actual possession remained with the landholder.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 10(3), 10(5) and 10(6) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, vesting under Section 10(3) does not itself transfer de facto possession. Section 10(5) provides for peaceful surrender or delivery following written notice, while Section 10(6) permits forcible possession if the person fails or refuses to comply. The notice requirements under subsections (5) and (6) are mandatory. The Court applied State of U.P. v. Hari Ram (2013) 4 SCC 280, which discusses the meaning of vesting with reference to Maharaj Singh v. State of U.P. (1977) 1 SCC 155 and Rajendra Kumar v. Kalyan (2000) 8 SCC 99.

rule.if: urban_land_ceiling_proceeding and vesting_notification_issued and holder_did_not_voluntarily_surrender and no_lawful_takeover_proved

predicates.urban_land_ceiling_proceeding: The dispute concerns proceedings to acquire excess vacant land under a statutory land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.vesting_notification_issued: The authority issued a notification treating the land as vested in the government.
predicates.holder_did_not_voluntarily_surrender: The landholder did not voluntarily deliver possession to the government or its representative.
predicates.no_lawful_takeover_proved: The authority did not establish that it obtained peaceful possession after notice or forcibly took possession through the required procedure.
predicates.de_facto_possession_remains_with_holder: The landholder continues to have actual possession of the land.

issues.definition: When land-ceiling proceedings produce a vesting notification but the holder does not surrender possession and no lawful takeover is proved, actual possession remains with the holder.

issues.legal_issue: Where the landholder retains actual possession when repeal of the land-ceiling scheme takes effect, the government cannot rely on statutory vesting or a later transfer receipt to continue possession proceedings.
material_facts: The state adopted the repeal legislation after the land-ceiling proceedings had begun.
The Principal Secretary stated that actual possession had not been taken under the land-ceiling statute before the repeal took effect.
The landholder had not surrendered possession, and there was no proof of a lawful takeover before repeal.
A possession receipt recording transfer to a development authority was executed after repeal without notice to the landholder.
The High Court had relegated the landholder to a civil suit concerning the land.
issues.conclusion: The landholder was entitled to the benefit of the repeal. The government could not retain the land on the basis of statutory vesting or the later possession receipt, and the notice and subsequent proceedings were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: The Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999 applies where actual possession was not taken before the repeal became effective. Applying State of U.P. v. Hari Ram (2013) 4 SCC 280 and its interpretation of Sections 10(3) to 10(6) of the 1976 Act, the Court held that de jure vesting alone does not establish that the government obtained actual possession. A later administrative transfer cannot cure the absence of actual possession before repeal.

predicates.appeal_challenges_land_ceiling_possessio: The proceeding is an appeal challenging government action to take or retain land under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.repeal_applies_to_state: The state is subject to the repeal of the land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.actual_possession_not_taken_before_repea: The government had not obtained actual possession of the land before the repeal took effect.
predicates.later_transfer_receipt_is_only_proof_of_: The only later record of possession is an administrative receipt transferring the land to another public authority, rather than proof of possession obtained from the landholder before repeal.
predicates.land_ceiling_proceedings_are_quashed: The notice and subsequent proceedings to take or retain the land under the repealed scheme are set aside.

issues.definition: If an appeal challenges land-ceiling possession action, the repeal applies, actual possession was not taken before repeal, and a later transfer receipt is the only proof of transfer, the proceedings are quashed.
